title: The Galois field trace decreases the Tate supremum norm
statement: Let $K$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, and let $T=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle$ ($d\ge0$) be a restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation] with its Gauss norm. Let $T\hookrightarrow B$ be an injective $K$-algebra map, where $B$ is a nonzero normal affinoid domain finite as a $T$-module and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ is finite Galois over $F=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$. A normal domain is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. Put $\rho_B(b)=\sup_{\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Max}B}|b\bmod\mathfrak m|$, using the unique absolute values on the finite residue fields as in [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. Then $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/F}(b)\in T$ and $\|\operatorname{Tr}_{L/F}(b)\|_G\le\rho_B(b)$ for every $b\in B$, where the field trace is the trace of the $F$-linear map $z\mapsto bz$ on $L$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4(b), PDF pp.2-3, trace contraction before the trace-dual-basis estimates. Read online 2026-10-24. Specialization to the finite Galois integral closure of a Tate algebra; uses maximal-ideal lying over. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], every $b\in B$ is integral over $T$. Mapping its monic equation into $L$ preserves that equation. By [lem-trf-field-trace-integrality], $\tau=\operatorname{Tr}_{L/F}(b)\in F$ is integral over $T$. Since $T$ is integrally closed in $F$ by [lem-trf-tate-integrally-closed], $\tau\in T$.

source.place: Theorem 4(b), printed/PDF pp.2-3, trace contraction; details reconstructed by Q142 using the cited algebraic and maximal-residue statements.

proof.text: Each $\sigma\in G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(L)$ fixes $T$. Apply $\sigma$ to a monic $T$-equation for $b$: it gives a monic $T$-equation, hence a monic $B$-equation, for $\sigma(b)$. Normality of $B$ in $L=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ gives $\sigma(b)\in B$. Doing the same for $\sigma^{-1}$ shows $\sigma(B)=B$. The restrictions are $K$-algebra automorphisms.

source.place: Theorem 4(b), printed/PDF pp.2-3, trace contraction; details reconstructed by Q142 using the cited algebraic and maximal-residue statements.

proof.text: Apply the functorial contraction in [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus] to $\sigma:B\to B$ and its inverse. It gives $\rho_B(\sigma b)\le\rho_B(b)\le\rho_B(\sigma b)$, so $\rho_B(\sigma b)=\rho_B(b)$. Both algebras are the given nonzero affinoid algebra.

source.place: Theorem 4(b), printed/PDF pp.2-3, trace contraction; details reconstructed by Q142 using the cited algebraic and maximal-residue statements.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-galois-trace-sum], $\tau=\sum_{\sigma\in G}\sigma b$ in $L$, hence in $B$. At each maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $B$, the residue absolute value is nonarchimedean: it extends $|\cdot|_K$, so $|k\cdot1|\le1$ for every integer $k$, hence $|x+y|^N\le\sum_{i=0}^N|x|^i|y|^{N-i}\le(N+1)\max(|x|,|y|)^N$ by the binomial theorem, and taking $N$-th roots as $N\to\infty$ gives $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$. This inequality, iterated over the finite sum, gives $|\tau\bmod\mathfrak n|\le\max_{\sigma\in G}|\sigma b\bmod\mathfrak n|\le\rho_B(b)$. The residue values and finite supremum exist by [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. Taking the supremum gives $\rho_B(\tau)\le\rho_B(b)$.

source.place: Theorem 4(b), printed/PDF pp.2-3, trace contraction; details reconstructed by Q142 using the cited algebraic and maximal-residue statements.

proof.text: For every maximal $\mathfrak m\subset T$, lying over [pqf-lem-lying-over] supplies a prime $\mathfrak n\subset B$ over it, since $T\hookrightarrow B$ is injective and integral by step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], $\mathfrak n$ is maximal. The inclusion $T/\mathfrak m\hookrightarrow B/\mathfrak n$ preserves absolute values: restricting the latter value extends $|\cdot|_K$, so uniqueness in [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus] identifies it with the former. Thus $|\tau\bmod\mathfrak m|\le\rho_B(\tau)$. Taking the supremum and using the same node's Tate comparison gives $\|\tau\|_G=\rho_T(\tau)\le\rho_B(\tau)\le\rho_B(b)$.

The item statement is unchanged and true. Tested on d=0, B=T, b=0 and scalar b where the characteristic divides [L:F]. Step 1: finite => integral (lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral), the trace is integral over T (lem-trf-field-trace-integrality, Algebra.isIntegral_trace at Mathlib/RingTheory/Trace/Basic.lean:162-171 with variables at 155-156, exact, no separability needed), and T is normal (new unsplit lem-trf-tate-integrally-closed, true since Tate algebras are UFDs; DAG search found no existing statement; the envelope node only covers its own T_i over an algebraically closed K). Step 2 is elementary: sigma(B)=B because B is normal. Step 3: the calculus node's contraction holds for any K-algebra map, with no continuity assumption, so applying it to sigma and sigma^{-1} gives equality. Step 4: trace equals the sum over the Galois group (trace_eq_sum_automorphisms at Basic.lean:263-264, exact). Step 5: lying over and prime-over-maximal (both Mathlib leaves) plus uniqueness of the residue values give rho_T<=rho_B, and the Tate clause gives rho_T equal to the Gauss norm; this is the correct direction.
